The earth has been so made that life can come into being within it; here it finds rest, and here it finds the means of growth. If the present form of this earth were not so, and its distances from the sun and the moon were not as they are, or its size were not what it is, or its elements and the elements in its atmosphere were not what they are, or the rotation of the earth on its axis were a little faster, or its revolution around the sun were faster than its present revolution, or the orbit of the moon around the earth were faster; these and other such conditions did not come into existence by mere chance, but have been brought into being with complete order and harmony. If any one of these conditions were to undergo even the slightest change, this earth would not be a place of "qarar" (stability), and neither humans nor anything else could live in it.

It is possible that the first audience of the Qur'an, from the words of Allah, "Amman ja'ala al-ardha qararا" (27:61), did not understand the things that we understand: "Who has made the earth a place of settlement?" But to this extent those people also understood that this earth is a place of settlement for life, and that life has been made possible upon it. They understood this truth in summary, and we understand it with further details. But none of those polytheists could claim that any of their deities shares with Allah in the creation of the earth. So this verse was sufficient for them, and along with the expansion of knowledge, the expansion of details has arisen within the meaning of this verse and will continue to arise. It is a miracle of the Qur'an's manner of expression and style of argument that a society backward in scientific terms benefited from it to the same extent as the advanced people of later times do today.

Amman ja'ala al-ardha qararan wa ja'ala khilalaha anhaara (27:61): "Who has made the earth a place of settlement and placed within it rivers flowing?" The rivers that Allah has set flowing upon the earth are in reality the arteries of life. They flow from the heights of this globe towards the directions of east, west, north and south, and they bring with them greenery, freshness and growth. Their formation is from the waters which Allah gathers in the earth, according to the natural conditions of each region. He who created this earth, in His plan placed the formation of clouds, the system of rain and the flow of rivers. Is there anyone who can say that any other than the Creator of the universe has a share in the arrangement of this system? Do we not see that great rivers are flowing upon this globe? This is a genuine question: who is it that caused these rivers to flow and run in this way? Is there any deity along with Allah?

Wa ja'ala lahha rawasiya (27:61): "and placed within it firm mountains." Rawasi means lofty mountains. They are fixed in their places and settled upon the earth. And very often rivers emerge from these very mountains, where the waters of rain gather and take the form of rivers, and then, because of these rivers, cracks and depths are formed in mountainous regions and become valleys, and from high places these rivers move with force towards low-lying areas. Here the manner of expression depicts flowing streams and rivers alongside the high and fixed mountains. It is a common feature of the Qur'anic portrayal that it presents contrasting scenes and meanings within a single verse. Here too, after the flowing rivers, standing mountains are shown.

Wa ja'ala bayna al-bahrayni hajizan (27:61): "and placed between the two seas a barrier." One sea is intensely salty and brackish, and the other is sweet and pleasant. Both are called "bahrayn" by way of "taghlib" (predominance), because the common substance of both is water, and the barrier between them is a natural barrier, such that the water of the sea does not mix with the water of the river and does not turn it salty. The details are that the surface of rivers is somewhat higher than the surface of the sea. When the waters of rivers fall into the sea, the surface of that water is higher than the surface of the sea. This river then continues to flow far across the surface of the sea; the sea does not spoil it. Now, even if this river water should fall below the level of the sea water, they still do not mix, because the sea water is denser than the river water. Because of this difference the two waters do not mix with each other but flow separately. This is the sunnah of Allah within His universe, and in this miraculous manner Allah has created His universe. Therefore the question is: who performed this miraculous work? Who else but Allah could be? "A-ilahun ma'a Allah" (27:61): if anyone can claim such a thing regarding anyone other than Allah, let him come forward. If not, then the wonders and designs of this universe are a clear proof that it has one Creator and that He is one.

Bal aktharahum la ya'lamun (27:61): "Rather, most of them are ignorant." Here too the mention of knowledge: "Without knowledge, God cannot be recognised." And as we explained in the summary of this surah and in the previous part, the central theme of this surah is knowledge; throughout the whole surah the importance of knowledge is emphasised.

Now the discourse turns from the observation of the universe to the valleys of the psychological world of man himself.

Now their conscience is touched. The inner misgivings present within their souls are stirred, and during the practical circumstances and important events of their lives, the states of their souls are placed before them. Those who, during a sea voyage, are surrounded by extremely difficult conditions, where apparent means come to an end and there appears to be no one who can come to their aid, and only hope in the help of Allah remains, and all supports are exhausted. A person looks in every direction and finds no support. No power of the earth is coming to their assistance. Those forces upon which a person, in his own thinking, has been relying for support all disappear one by one. Every power from which any expectation was held gives way. In such despairing circumstances, human nature awakens once again. The person turns toward the power that is the true power. Now the person turns to Allah, although before this, in his normal circumstances, he had forgotten Allah. For it is Allah alone who gives aid to a helpless person when he, having become without support, calls upon Him, and it is Allah who then delivers him from difficulties. He grants peace and security and rescues him from that hardship.

When people are in peace, well-being and prosperity, they are immersed in heedlessness. They forget the Divine Being. Then they seek help and support from some power among the powers of the earth. But when hardship comes and they are surrounded by extreme anguish, the veils of heedlessness are lifted, and at that time they turn back to their Lord, humbly and imploringly. Although they were heedless and obstinate.

The Qur'an draws the attention of deniers and the obstinate to the truth that is within their own nature. The Qur'an presents this matter in an environment in which are displayed the scenes of the creation of the heavens and the earth, the sending down of water from the sky, the growth of fresh gardens and orchards upon the earth, the stability of this globe, the setting of mountains upon it, the flowing and running of rivers and streams within it, and the barriers between two kinds of water in the sea. Then, by presenting a turbulent and distressing situation at sea, it has been made clear that in such circumstances no one calls upon anyone other than Allah, and that this too is a reality, just like the aforementioned cosmic Creator. Those were cosmic realities, and this one concerns the psychological world of man.

Now, by bringing them out even from the world of their psychology, Allah the Exalted brings them to a practical state of their life.

Who is it that makes you successors (khulafa') of the earth (27:62), "and makes you successors upon the earth." Who is it that created man here, granted him superiority over all creatures? After that, one after another, He continued granting authority over this earth to some, while some fell into decline and others attained ascendancy. This one fell and that one rose.

Is it not Allah who, in accordance with the laws of nature, gave you life on this earth, and then bestowed upon you powers by which you became worthy of the caliphate of Allah on this globe, and then prepared you here for this great office? He made the earth a place of settlement for you, and made every thing in it supportive and harmonious with your life, so that every thing on the earth became a means of sustaining life for you. And if it were the case that one of the essential elements of the earth were removed, then all humans, indeed all living things, would be destroyed in an instant, and for the future the existence of anything here would become impossible.

Finally, there is this: it is Allah who is the Being who created life and death, and raised one generation after another. If Allah were to keep the coming generations in the same way, and new generations kept coming into being, there would not be room on this globe even to place a pin. The current of life would be very slow, human thinking would be extremely sluggish, because with the coming into existence of fresh generations, fresh ideas and fresh thoughts also arrive. People conduct new experiments and make new efforts in the struggle of life. They discover new ways of living, and now the situation is that the struggle between old and new people takes place only on the field of thought and consciousness. And if all the earlier people were also still alive, there would be physical conflict between old and new people as well, and instead of the cart of life moving forward, it would fall victim to mutual contradictions and clashes.

These are all psychological realities, just as the cosmic realities mentioned earlier were. Who is it that brought these realities into being and made you successors? Is there anyone besides Allah? Is there any god with Allah (27:62), "Is there a god along with Allah?"

The truth is that people forget realities. When they emerge from the difficulties of the sea, they forget everything. Their nature also falls asleep, and they become heedless, although within their own souls and in the universe spread around them, realities exist.

Qalilan ma tadhakkarun (27:62), "How little you reflect." If a person keeps realities in mind and continually reflects upon them, he will always remain attached to Allah and will keep listening to the call of his nature. He will never be heedless of his Lord, and will never associate anyone with his Lord.

After this, some other realities are presented from the lives of people. These relate to human activities upon this globe and to those observations that are repeated at every moment.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 27, verse 63:

Is it not He Who guides you in the darkness of the land and the sea? ... [﴿Am yahdeekum...﴾] ... Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him (27:63).

All people travel by sea, and among them were those who were the first addressees of the Qur'an. These people travel the routes of land and sea, and they have traveled, and still travel, through the darkness of land and sea according to their experience and knowledge. In these journeys they find the right paths. Who is it that shows human beings the straight way in these journeys? Who gave humanity this intellect and understanding by which they perceive these routes? Who gave the knowledge of the stars? Then who gave the power to discover instruments? And who revealed experiences and signs? Who is the Being that created harmony between human nature and the nature of the universe, and paved the way for humans to reach the nature of the universe? Who is it that gave humans, through the ears, the power to perceive sounds? Who is it that gave humans, through the eye, the power to observe from afar? And who is it that, through the five senses, granted humans the ability to know all perceptible things? Then He gave humans the power of reason, through which humans comprehend things more subtle than the senses. Then He gave them the powers to draw conclusions from the experiences of the senses, and to derive truths through intuition and inspiration.

﴿A-ilahun maʿa Allah﴾ (27:63): "Is there another god along with Allah?"

﴿Wa man yursilu al-riyaha bushran bayna yaday rahmatih﴾ (27:63): "And who is it that sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy?" These winds, concerning whose celestial causes much has been said and will be said, are those which Allah created on this earth from the very first day. And just as they blow, from the first day they have had this arrangement: they carry the clouds on their backs from one place and bring glad tidings to human beings of that which sustains life, namely water.

The question is: who created these winds, these clouds, and this system of rain in its present form? And then, who sends the cool winds before the clouds and rain?

﴿A-ilahun maʿa Allah﴾ (27:63): "Is there another god along with Allah?"

﴿Taʿala Allah ʿamma yushrikun﴾ (27:63): "Exalted is Allah far above what they associate with Him."

﴿Is He not the One who originates creation, then repeats it?﴾ (27:64) (Passage begins mid-verse.)

The beginning of this universe and its creatures is a reality that no one can deny. The problem of the creation of the universe cannot be solved without acknowledging the existence of Allah, the One, because the very existence of this universe necessitates that Allah exists. Those people in the world who have tried to solve the problem of the existence of this universe without acknowledging the existence of God, although in the very existence of this universe a purposeful will, an intention and a plan is evident, have failed miserably in solving the problem of the universe. And the oneness of Allah is established because in all the signs of this universe unity is visible: its management is one, its destiny is one, and in the whole scheme of this universe there is such coherence and harmony that, without accepting that it has one creator, there is no alternative.

This was the beginning. As for the matter that Allah Almighty will repeat the creation of this universe, all the disbelievers and polytheists were in doubt about it. But the person who reaches the conclusion regarding the beginning of this universe that it is the creation of a being possessing will and management, and that it is one because of the unity and coherence found within this universe, for him it is not a difficult matter to accept that this Being will recreate him, so that those who come into this world will find the full recompense of their deeds there. This is because in this world a person receives reward and punishment for good and bad deeds, but that reward and punishment are not complete. Therefore, for complete retribution (mukafat-e-amal, the principle that deeds are recompensed) it is necessary that there be a world in which there is complete reward and punishment. Without this, the completion of the life of this world is simply not possible. Therefore the affirmation of a coming life is necessary, in which complete harmony and complete perfection will be attained. The question is: according to the principle of retribution, why was reward and punishment not carried out in this world? The answer is that it is due to wisdoms which only the Creator of the universe knows well, because the secrets of His creation are all with the Creator alone, and these are unseen secrets of which Allah has not informed human beings.

It is according to this principle that the verse asks who originated this universe and who will recreate it. Obviously the answer to this is that there is no one.

﴿Is there any other god with Allah?﴾ (27:64)

The matter of providing sustenance is related both to the beginning of creation and is also connected to the repetition of creation. The provision for the sustenance of Allah's servants is entirely manifest and evident, in the form of plants and in the form of animals. Water and air are necessary for eating, drinking and breathing. The mineral deposits and metals of the earth are also beneficial and necessary for human beings, among which magnetic force and electrical force are very important. Within this universe Allah has placed for human life, besides these, countless and unlimited other forces which are necessary for human life, but human beings do not yet have knowledge of them. From time to time Allah Almighty informs human beings about them.

How is sustenance provided to human beings from the heavens? In this world, light is provided to human beings from the heavens, heat is provided, rain is provided, and all other things whose source lies in the heavens. And the high ranks and great rewards which Allah Almighty will give to the people of faith on the Day of Resurrection are also, in a spiritual sense, a heavenly sustenance, because the Qur'an also descends from the heights and elevation and descends for elevation.

Here Allah Almighty, after creation and the repetition of creation, has mentioned that Allah provides sustenance to His creatures from the heavens. This is because there is a clear connection between the sustenance of the earth and the beginning of creation. All creation is alive because of the sustenance of the earth. And the connection of these sustenances with the Hereafter is also clear from the beginning of creation. In worldly life, human beings need the sustenance and means of living from the heavens, and in the Hereafter these blessings will be given to human beings in the form of their complete recompense (jaza wa fa-faq, "full recompense"). Therefore the connection of the beginning of creation with the sustenance of the heavens and the earth is clear, and the word of God is interlinked in a wonderfully amazing manner. The beginning of creation and the repetition of creation are in reality self-evident truths. Likewise, the provision of sustenance for human beings and all creatures from the heavens and the earth is in fact well-known truths, but the condition of people is that they do not reflect upon these truths. Therefore the Qur'an addresses them in this manner with great force and in the style of challenge (tahaddi).

﴿Say: Bring your proof, if you are truthful.﴾ (27:64)

Indeed, even at that time the opponents were unable to bring any proof of this kind, and to this day no one has been able to bring any proof of this kind. This is the style of the Qur'an's discourse in doctrinal discussions. The Qur'an presents the sights and observations of the universe. It presents the realities present within the human self. In this way, the logic which the Qur'an presents extends its scope over this entire universe. It turns human thought and vision throughout the whole universe. It polishes human nature so that the human mind and human nature themselves may arrive at a conclusion which is clear and simple, and so that human consciousness may be vibrant and its intuitive faculty may be functioning well, because the proofs are present within the human self and human nature itself, but due to heedlessness and forgetfulness people do not turn their attention to them, and disbelief and denial throw veils over these proofs. Thus, through these intuitive and cosmic proofs, and on the strength of this natural logic, the noble Qur'an leads human beings to the great realities present within this universe and within the human self. These realities become so clear that they do not retain those doubts and suspicions which are established through dry logical reasoning by means of the minor and major premises (sughra and kubra). This is because this bookish logic came to us through Greek culture and became part of our scholastic theology (ilm al-kalam), although its style was not Qur'anic. It distanced us from Qur'anic logic. Having traveled through the valleys of the self and the horizons, and having established intuitively the belief in tawhid and the negation of shirk, the noble Qur'an now leads us into the valley which is hidden within the unseen world, and whose circumstances only that Creator and Manager can tell who created this universe, namely, what will happen after death, how the Hereafter will be. This is because it is one of the unseen matters of Allah. And the Qur'an, intuitive logic, divine guidance and human nature all testify to its occurrence, and human beings are incapable, through knowledge and perception, of determining when this hour will come.

﴿Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah; and they do not know when they will be raised.﴾ (27:65)

"Say to them: none in the heavens and the earth has knowledge of the unseen except Allah, and they (your deities) do not even know when they will be raised. Rather, the knowledge of the Hereafter has disappeared from these people; rather, they are in doubt about it; rather, they are blind to it. These deniers say: 'When we and our fathers have become dust, will we really be brought out from graves? We have been given these reports, and our forefathers were also given them before, but these are nothing but fables which we have been hearing from earlier times.' Say: just travel in the earth and see what the end of the criminals has been. O Prophet (ﷺ), do not grieve over their condition, nor let your heart be constricted by their schemes. They say: 'When will this threat be fulfilled, if you are truthful?' Say: it may be that a part of the punishment for which you are hastening has come close to you. In truth, your Lord is indeed bountiful to people, but most people do not give thanks. Surely your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they display. There is no hidden thing in the heavens and the earth which is not in a manifest Book."

Belief in the unseen, being raised after death, and accounting for the deeds of the whole life are a fundamental element within Islamic beliefs. From the Islamic perspective, no system of life can be established without these beliefs. Therefore it is incumbent upon every Muslim to believe in the coming world, where there is complete recompense for deeds and complete balance between action and its reward. This belief should be lodged in the human heart, the human self should be sensitive to it, and all human activities in this world should be founded upon the belief that one will have to give a full account of one's life in the Hereafter.

In its long history, humanity has adopted strange and wondrous positions regarding the belief in the Hereafter in contrast to various messengers, although this belief is very simple and appears very necessary to one who reflects. Whenever a messenger came and called people to the belief in the Hereafter, people considered this call very strange and wondrous. Yet this universe existed, this colorful life existed upon it, and they themselves existed. Was it difficult to bring these wonders into existence the first time, or was it difficult to repeat them a second time? This is why people have always turned away from the call of those who warn about the Hereafter. They kept babbling about this call and went on increasing in disbelief and denial.

The establishment of the Hour is an unseen matter which only Allah knows, and knowledge of it belongs to Allah alone. The disbelievers always demanded of the prophets that they specify the time of the occurrence of the Resurrection. When they did not get this certainty, they denied it and considered it merely a tale of earlier times, saying that this is a matter which has been spoken of since ancient times but has not yet occurred.

Here it is first stated that your knowledge regarding the Hereafter is limited, and the occurrence of the Hereafter is one of those unseen matters of which human beings have no knowledge.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 27, verses 65–66:

"Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah. And they do not perceive when they will be resurrected." (27: 65)

"Rather, their knowledge has fallen short concerning the Hereafter. Rather, they are in doubt about it. Rather, they are blind to it." (27: 66)

From the beginning of creation, man has been confronted with this hidden unseen. Human knowledge cannot go beyond a certain limit. Behind the veils that hang before the unseen, he cannot peer beyond. He can acquire only as much knowledge of the unseen as Allah grants him the ability to acquire, and it is for man's good that Allah has kept him deprived of knowledge of the future. Had Allah seen any good for man in it, He would surely have granted him complete knowledge of the unseen world.

Allah has given man only as much power and capacity as enables him to fulfil his duties in this world as Allah's khalifah (vicegerent) on earth. These duties are not ordinary duties. Beyond this, Allah has not given man further unseen powers. Had man been given such a power by which he could tear through the veils of the future and obtain information, then no increase in his powers would have been possible through it, beyond those by which he is carrying out his work here as khalifah. Rather, the placing of veils before future events is itself the spur to this desire for knowledge. Thus he keeps striving to dig into and search out the hidden future on his own. In this way he seeks the secrets hidden within the earth. He cleaves the breast of the sea. He runs far through the spaces of the sky. He uncovers the hidden secrets of this universe, and he keeps discovering the secrets of good for mankind. He extracts materials and elements from the earth, performs chemical processes on their composition and form, and brings changes to the varieties and modes of life. In this way he is playing a most important role in the construction and development of this earth, and he is discharging, with full responsibility, the duties with which Allah entrusted him when He gave him the office of khilafah.

Man alone has not been deprived of the knowledge of the unseen. Whatever creation exists in the heavens and the earth has been deprived of it, whether they are angels, jinn, or any other creation that is within Allah's knowledge. None of them has been given knowledge of the unseen, because they had no need for it. Therefore, all unseen knowledge and all events that are to occur are known to Allah alone.

"Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah" (27: 65). This is a definitive text (nass qati'), and in its presence no one can claim knowledge of the unseen, nor is there any room to believe in superstitions and fables in this regard.

After the general negation of the unseen, the particular negation of the establishment of the Resurrection is now made, because after the belief in tawhid, the major dispute between Muslims and the people of shirk was precisely this. "And they do not perceive when they will be raised" (27: 65). That is, those whom you worship are not even aware of the Resurrection. When they have no awareness of the Resurrection, how could they have knowledge of it? Thus the establishment of the Resurrection is among those hidden matters of which no one in the heavens and the earth has knowledge; rather, their knowledge of the Hereafter is very limited.

"Rather, their knowledge of the Hereafter has been lost" (27: 66). It has gone very far within its own limits, and people's reaching it has remained distant, and veils have intervened between it and them.

"Rather, they are in doubt about it" (27: 66). These people do not have certainty about the coming of this Resurrection. It is far from the case that they would have any knowledge of the time of its coming, or that they are awaiting its occurrence.

"Rather, they are in doubt about it" (27: 66). These people do not have certainty about the coming of this Resurrection. It is far from the case that they would have any knowledge of the time of its coming, or that they are awaiting its occurrence.

"Rather, they are blind to it" (27: 66). That is, they are blind concerning it. Nothing regarding the Resurrection appears to them. Nor will they recall anything about its nature. Their distance from it is greater than the first and the second distances.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 27, verse 67:

﴿And those who disbelieve say: "When we have become dust, and our fathers too, shall we really be brought forth?"﴾ (27:67). The belief of the disbelievers was this: when we die and our bodies in the graves become dust and scatter, just as it is observed that all the dead, some time after burial, become like this, and bodies remain preserved only rarely. When we too become like this, and our forefathers have also gone that way, shall we then be taken out again and be raised to life when the particles of our bodies have already mixed with the earth? This is indeed a very strange matter. They say this, and their conception of matter makes the concept of the life of the Hereafter difficult for them. Yet they forget that they were created before, and before that creation they were nothing at all. No one knew that the cells and particles within the body, from which this structure of their life has been built, where they had been gathered from. They were scattered around the earth, in the depths of the seas, or were flying in the atmospheres of this universe. Earth was taken, particles were taken from the winds, and who lifted the water particles from which clouds and which clouds carried them? And some particles came from the sun. Then, through breathing, through plants, through the milk and flesh of animals, through vapours into which they enter, and through drinking, those things which become part of the body; then the body is affected by the heat of the sun. All these various things, the number of which only Allah knows, are gathered into the human body, and this human being reaches this point from that small microscopic egg. This egg is attached to the walls of the womb, and on growing up, and on dying, all these components are gathered within the shroud. This is its first creation. So what is surprising about Allah raising this creation again from the grave? But those people did say this in any case, and some of this kind of people still exist today who say such things. They used to say these things, and after that, to express further mockery and disapproval, they would say:

These people knew that before them, messengers had likewise warned their forefathers about the Last Day and spoken of reckoning and of resurrection and gathering. From this it becomes clear that the belief in the Hereafter was not an entirely new belief for the Arabs. It was not that they did not understand the meaning of resurrection after death; rather, their objection was that these promises had been made for centuries and had not been fulfilled. On this basis they used to mock this belief, and they would say that these are only the stories of the ancients, which Muhammad (ﷺ) keeps relating. These people were heedless of the fact that the Hour of resurrection has a set time. It can neither come sooner because of anyone's haste, nor be delayed because of anyone's negligence. It will come at a known and appointed time, and its knowledge has been kept hidden from the creatures of both the heavens and the earth. The Prophet (ﷺ) said exactly this to Jibril (peace be upon him) when he asked him about the Hour:

ما المسؤل عنها باعلم من السائل "The one who is asked about it knows no more than the one who asks."

Here, these people are directed to the places of slaughter of those who were destroyed before them, who denied the truth, and whom the Qur'an here describes as the criminals (al-mujrimun).

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 27, verse 69:

﴿Say: "Travel through the earth and see what was the end of the criminals."﴾ (27:69) "". Here, through this guidance of travelling in the earth (sayr fi al-ard), the scope of their thinking is broadened. For no society of humanity is cut off from the chain of humanity. The laws (sunan) that Allah has placed for humanity are unalterable for all. The conditions that the criminals of earlier human societies faced, those who come after them will inevitably face conditions similar to them. For the laws of Allah are unalterable; they show no leniency to anyone. And by travelling and moving about the earth, the sphere of the information of the human self becomes very wide. The human mind becomes illuminated, and during travelling in the earth moments come upon a person such that the person's conscience becomes illuminated. The Qur'an repeatedly draws the attention of humans to the unalterable principles and laws (sunan) of this universe, and invites humans to reflect carefully on these laws, or in other words on the chain of cause and effect (silsila-i-illat o ma'lul), to observe its links one after another, so that your life remains connected and joined with the collective life of humanity, and the bounds of your thinking acquire breadth. Your thinking should not be limited, narrow, or cut off from the current of life.

After these directions, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is now instructed to wash his hands of these people, to leave them to whatever end they may meet, just as criminals before them met such an end in history. And the deceptions these people are carrying out against the Islamic movement will not be able to cause it any harm. Moreover, out of sympathy, do not be distressed on their account, because you have fulfilled the right of preaching and guidance and have explained to them thoroughly.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 27, verse 70:

﴿And do not grieve over them, and do not be distressed by their scheming.﴾ (27:70)

This verse shows how deeply sensitive the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was, and how much concern he felt for the evil end awaiting his people. For he knew what became of the nations that denied their messengers. This verse also shows that, at that time, these people were weaving webs of deceit against the Prophet (ﷺ), and they wanted to uproot the Muslims and the call of Islam from their very roots. The Messenger (ﷺ) was greatly troubled by this.

Further examples of their views about resurrection after death are presented here. They would mock the evil end with which they were warned, both in this world and in the Hereafter, and they would say:

They say, "When will this promise come to pass, if you are truthful?" (27:71)

These people would say this whenever they were warned of a fate like that of earlier nations, the ruins of whose settlements they passed by day and night: for example, the town of Sodom, the people of Lot; the traces of Thamud at al-Hijr; the remains of 'Ad in the region of al-Ahqaf; and the ruins of the people of Sheba, which were destroyed after the flood of al-Arim (Sayl al-Arim). They would say: "Tell us definitely when that punishment about which you frighten us will come. If you are truthful, tell us what kind of punishment it will be and when it will happen."

Here, too, the reply is given in the same contemptuous manner, and in extreme brevity.

Say: "It may be that some of what you seek to hasten is close behind you," (27:72)

Thus Allah and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) instil fear in their hearts through the thought of punishment and destruction. That is, it may be that this punishment is as near to you, and as attached to you, as the second rider sitting behind a person on a camel is to him, so close that he is right there, and yet you are not aware of it. You are hastening because of your heedlessness and ignorance, while it is sitting behind you and will suddenly seize you. Because of such a sudden seizure from the rear, a person's whole body trembles. Likewise, this punishment may seize you while you are busy with mockery. Who knows what the future and the next moment hold? For the unseen of the future is hidden. There are veils between us and it. Who knows what lies behind the veils? Sometimes, at a distance of only a few paces, there is a frightening situation. The intelligent person remains alert at all times, fears, and stays ready at all times and for every kind of circumstance, knowing that any eventuality may arise.

And indeed your Lord is full of bounty toward mankind, but most of them do not give thanks. (27:73)

Divine favour is evident: Allah grants people respite and postpones the punishment from them, although they are sinful and guilty and persist in their sins. This is because the hope of their reform still remains, and postponing the punishment is itself a bounty of Allah. Thanks for it is due, but most people, instead of giving thanks, respond with mockery and insolence, and they continue on in their misguidance without reflection or understanding.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 27, verse 74:

﴿وَإِنَّ رَبَّكَ لَيَعْلَمُ مَا تُكِنُّ صُدُورُهُمْ وَمَا يُعْلِنُونَ﴾ [27:74]

"Allah does not bring the punishment upon them and keeps postponing it, even though He knows well what these people are concealing in their hearts and what they are displaying. This passage concludes with the point that nothing in the heavens and the earth is hidden or concealed from Allah."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 27, verse 75:

وما من غائبۃ فی السماء والارض الا فی کتب مبین (27: 75) Thought and imagination now move into the wide field of the heavens and the earth. The hidden secrets within the heavens and the earth are countless: countless mysteries, countless powers, countless wonders, all of them bound to the knowledge and the established law (nāmūs) of Allah. Nothing is hidden from the knowledge of Allah, nor is anything absent from His knowledge. The division into "present" and "absent" is a division of human knowledge. The reminder of this surah is centred on knowledge. Throughout the whole surah there are indications towards knowledge, and at the conclusion of this lesson this is the final indication.

With reference to the absolute knowledge of Allah, here the knowledge of Allah, by bringing forward decisive and clear-cut matters in the Qur'an, has resolved those issues of the Children of Israel over which they had been in disagreement for centuries. This Qur'an is a part and a sample of the knowledge of Allah, and it is one of the bounties of Allah. It is, for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), a degree of consolation that he should continue calling these people towards this final decision of Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 27, verses 76–81:

[Qur'anic text: ان ھذا القران ۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ لا من یؤمن بایتنا فھم مسلمون (81)]

Among the Christians there was sharp disagreement about Jesus (peace be upon him) and his mother. One group held that Jesus was merely a human being. Some said that the words God used about him, "Father," "Son," and "Holy Spirit," actually refer to different names for the Divine Being. According to this group, God is composed of three hypostases (aqanim): the Father, the Son (ibn), and the Holy Spirit (ruh al-qudus). Since the Son was Jesus (peace be upon him), God, who was in the form of the Lord, descended in the form of the Holy Spirit, took the form of a human being within Mary, and this God was then born from Mary in human form.

One group said that the Son is not eternal (azali) as the Father is eternal; rather, he was created before the world. Therefore he is of a lower rank than the Lord and is obedient to the Lord's command.

Some people said that the Holy Spirit is not a hypostasis (aqnum). The Council of Nicaea of 325 decided this, and the Council of Constantinople of 381 confirmed that the Son and the Holy Spirit are equal to the Father and are also part of the unity of the Godhead (lahut). These sons too were born in eternity, whereas the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Lord. And the Council of Toledo of 589 decided that the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Son. On this point a divergence arose between the Eastern and Western churches, which remains a point of disagreement to this day.

When the Qur'an was revealed, it made a decisive statement: he is a word which Allah sent to Mary, and a spirit from Allah, and he is a human being.

﴿He is nothing but a servant upon whom We bestowed favour, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel﴾ (43:59). This was the decisive word on which they differed.

Likewise, among the Children of Israel there was disagreement about the crucifixion of Jesus (peace be upon him). Some believed that he was crucified, died, was buried, and after three days rose from his grave and was lifted up to the heavens. Others believed that one of his disciples, Yahuda, was made to resemble Jesus (peace be upon him) and was crucified, because that man had betrayed Jesus and pointed out his location to the authorities, and so Jesus was arrested. Others believed that one of his disciples, Shimon, was made to resemble him, and he was arrested. The Qur'an stated the reality: ﴿And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them﴾ (4:157). And elsewhere the Qur'an said: ﴿O Jesus, I will take you and raise you to Myself and purify you﴾ (3:55). This was the decisive statement concerning Jesus.

Before this, the Jews had also altered the law of the Torah; many rulings had been distorted. When the Qur'an came, it stated the original law: ﴿And We prescribed for them therein: life for life, eye for eye, nose for nose, ear for ear, tooth for tooth, and for all wounds, equal retribution (qisas)﴾ (5:45).

The Qur'an presented the facts of the history of the Children of Israel and their prophets, and it separated and cleared away the stories, tales and fables that they had wrongly mixed with those facts. These fables were such that no prophet could emerge from them innocent and pure. Some well-known examples of their fables are these: they accused Abraham (peace be upon him) of presenting his wife as his sister before Abimelech, king of Palestine, and Pharaoh, king of Egypt; according to them, Abraham wished to gain a high position in their eyes. And Jacob (peace be upon him), whose name was Israel, obtained the blessings of Abraham from his father Isaac through trickery, deceit and theft, although these blessings belonged to his elder brother Esau. And concerning Lot (peace be upon him), their narrations say that his two daughters, so that his lineage would not pass to others, did such a thing, and what the girls desired came to pass. And David saw a beautiful woman in his palace and learned that she was the wife of his soldier; then he sent that soldier on a deadly mission so that he could take the wife. And Solomon turned toward worship of Lo'l merely to please one of his wives, because he loved her and could not refuse her demand. These were their accusations against their prophets.

When the Qur'an was revealed, Allah declared the innocence of all the prophets and removed these delusions and fables from the lives of the prophets, because these delusions had been inserted by the Jews and Christians into their own books. In particular, the Qur'an negated all the false things attributed to the person of Jesus (peace be upon him) and Mary (peace be upon her), and stated the correct teachings that come from Allah. In this sense the Qur'an has been called muhaymin over the earlier scriptures: it judges the differences among them and makes the decisive statement on all disputed and argumentative matters.

﴿And it is a guidance and mercy for the believers﴾ (27:77). This is the guidance that protects the believers from error and disagreement. It gives them a way of life, supports them on the path of life, and gives them teachings and views that are in harmony with the divine laws (sunan Ilahiyyah) present throughout this universe. This Qur'an is also mercy along with guidance. It saves human beings from doubt, restlessness, anxiety and uncertainty, and protects them from weak views that change day after day, that have no firm footing and cannot stand on their own. Its teachings bring a person, through satisfaction, to the shelter of Allah's mercy and the abode of tranquility. In this way a person harmonizes with his environment, his society and his own thoughts, and lives in peace, and in the Hereafter becomes deserving of Allah's pleasure and great reward. The Qur'anic method for training the human soul and shaping it again according to the laws of nature is a unique method. According to this method, a person lives his life in accordance with those laws of nature which also operate in this universe, and thus his life passes with great tranquility and in a natural way. There is no pretence or artificiality in it. As a result of the Islamic method of training, a person feels contentment even in the depths of his life, and this is a very great wealth. This contentment is attained because, under the Islamic system of training, a person's life does not conflict with the laws of nature, nor does a person conflict with the laws of nature and this universe that moves according to them, nor does human morality conflict with these laws of nature, provided that a person can understand the laws of nature and the principles well, and recognizes the points where human personality and this universe are connected. And a person reaches the conclusion that there is no contradiction between human nature, cosmic nature and the Islamic system of life, but that they are mutually proportionate and in harmony. This is the great peace that is established between the human personality and the vast universe spread around a person, and as a result of this peace human society lives a most tranquil life. And this is the mercy to which the Qur'an points. This is the broader meaning of divine mercy.

After these indications that the Qur'an resolves most of the doctrinal issues of the Children of Israel, removes their disagreements, and gives the believers a natural system of life, granting them great tranquility and peace, Allah now consoles the Prophet ﷺ: his people are unjustly disputing with him. Allah will soon decide this as well, with a decision that no one can reject, because Allah's decisions are based on realities and correct knowledge.

﴿So put your trust in Allah; indeed you are upon the manifest truth﴾ (27:79). Allah has made it obligatory upon Himself to support the truth and make it prevail, just as His other laws operating in this universe are necessary and unalterable. These laws do not stop; likewise truth prevails. However, owing to certain hidden wisdoms of Allah, this victory sometimes comes late, and only Allah knows those wisdoms. There are purposes known only to Allah, yet these sunnah are fulfilled without fail and in the end truth attains victory. This is Allah's promise, and it is never broken. A person's faith cannot be complete unless he believes in the unalterability of this sunnah. The meaning is that for the success of truth there is a time appointed with Allah, and before that time this success cannot come. If people are hasty, that is their own mistake.

The Prophet ﷺ faced great difficulties from his people: they quarrelled over every matter, were obstinate and stubborn, and out of mere enmity they did not accept even things that were evident at first sight. Despite the Messenger's ﷺ struggle and his extremely clear proclamation and preaching, they insisted on disbelief, and they ignored the repeated address of the Qur'an. In the face of all this, he is consoled that he has fulfilled the duty of conveying the message and has committed no fault, but it is those who are alive, whose ears are receptive, who listen to words. The dead never listen. The minds of the dead have died, and they become devoid of reflection. Therefore the dead neither believe nor hear. Your people's hearts and minds have died; hence to speak to them is now as good as not speaking. There is no path left before them to return to guidance. Now leave them to their misguidance, their rebellion and their straying.

﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn away and flee, nor can you guide the blind out of their straying. You can make hear only those who believe in Our signs and then submit﴾ (27:80–81).

The Qur'an has portrayed the intellectual and psychological condition of these people in a most remarkable manner. It has given a tangible form to intangible meanings. Heart's stagnation, spiritual deadness, dullness of mind and decline of consciousness are described as if these people were dead and deaf, and the Messenger were calling them while they neither hear nor respond, because the dead neither hear, nor have awareness, nor can respond. Another tangible image is of a person who is deaf, hears nothing at all, and does not even turn his face toward the one calling him, but goes in the opposite direction. No matter how loudly you call such a person, he will not hear. At times the Qur'an presents them in the form of the blind: how can a blind person walk on the right path when he cannot see anything at his next step? In these verses all these forms have been presented in a most embodied and personal manner.

Now, in contrast to these dead, deaf and blind people, stand the believers. They are alive, they hear, and they see.

﴿You can make hear only those who believe in Our signs and then submit﴾ (27:81). That is, you can make hear only those who have life, the faculty of hearing and the faculty of sight. Speak only to such people. These are the signs of life, and consciousness exists among living people. Only those who hear and see can accept the call, and it is the believers alone in whom life, hearing and sight are found. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ worked upon such people; they accepted the call and surrendered.

Islam is a very simple religion, easy to understand, and very close to the sound nature (fitrah salimah). A sound heart and a sound nature accept the Islamic call as soon as they encounter it and submit. They do not then indulge in idle talk and disputation. This is the picture of the believers, and it is such people who should be invited. Such people hasten toward the call as soon as they hear it and believe immediately. Leaving the dead in their place, the caller should reach those people who are ready to accept.

[Qur'anic text: ان ھذا القران ۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔۔ لا من یؤمن بایتنا فھم مسلمون (81)]

Among the Christians there was sharp disagreement about Jesus (peace be upon him) and his mother. One group held that Jesus was merely a human being. Some said that the words God used about him, "Father," "Son," and "Holy Spirit," actually refer to different names for the Divine Being. According to this group, God is composed of three hypostases (aqanim): the Father, the Son (ibn), and the Holy Spirit (ruh al-qudus). Since the Son was Jesus (peace be upon him), God, who was in the form of the Lord, descended in the form of the Holy Spirit, took the form of a human being within Mary, and this God was then born from Mary in human form.

One group said that the Son is not eternal (azali) as the Father is eternal; rather, he was created before the world. Therefore he is of a lower rank than the Lord and is obedient to the Lord's command.

Some people said that the Holy Spirit is not a hypostasis (aqnum). The Council of Nicaea of 325 decided this, and the Council of Constantinople of 381 confirmed that the Son and the Holy Spirit are equal to the Father and are also part of the unity of the Godhead (lahut). These sons too were born in eternity, whereas the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Lord. And the Council of Toledo of 589 decided that the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Son. On this point a divergence arose between the Eastern and Western churches, which remains a point of disagreement to this day.

When the Qur'an was revealed, it made a decisive statement: he is a word which Allah sent to Mary, and a spirit from Allah, and he is a human being.

﴿He is nothing but a servant upon whom We bestowed favour, and We made him an example for the Children of Israel﴾ (43:59). This was the decisive word on which they differed.

Likewise, among the Children of Israel there was disagreement about the crucifixion of Jesus (peace be upon him). Some believed that he was crucified, died, was buried, and after three days rose from his grave and was lifted up to the heavens. Others believed that one of his disciples, Yahuda, was made to resemble Jesus (peace be upon him) and was crucified, because that man had betrayed Jesus and pointed out his location to the authorities, and so Jesus was arrested. Others believed that one of his disciples, Shimon, was made to resemble him, and he was arrested. The Qur'an stated the reality: ﴿And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them﴾ (4:157). And elsewhere the Qur'an said: ﴿O Jesus, I will take you and raise you to Myself and purify you﴾ (3:55). This was the decisive statement concerning Jesus.

Before this, the Jews had also altered the law of the Torah; many rulings had been distorted. When the Qur'an came, it stated the original law: ﴿And We prescribed for them therein: life for life, eye for eye, nose for nose, ear for ear, tooth for tooth, and for all wounds, equal retribution (qisas)﴾ (5:45).

The Qur'an presented the facts of the history of the Children of Israel and their prophets, and it separated and cleared away the stories, tales and fables that they had wrongly mixed with those facts. These fables were such that no prophet could emerge from them innocent and pure. Some well-known examples of their fables are these: they accused Abraham (peace be upon him) of presenting his wife as his sister before Abimelech, king of Palestine, and Pharaoh, king of Egypt; according to them, Abraham wished to gain a high position in their eyes. And Jacob (peace be upon him), whose name was Israel, obtained the blessings of Abraham from his father Isaac through trickery, deceit and theft, although these blessings belonged to his elder brother Esau. And concerning Lot (peace be upon him), their narrations say that his two daughters, so that his lineage would not pass to others, did such a thing, and what the girls desired came to pass. And David saw a beautiful woman in his palace and learned that she was the wife of his soldier; then he sent that soldier on a deadly mission so that he could take the wife. And Solomon turned toward worship of Lo'l merely to please one of his wives, because he loved her and could not refuse her demand. These were their accusations against their prophets.

When the Qur'an was revealed, Allah declared the innocence of all the prophets and removed these delusions and fables from the lives of the prophets, because these delusions had been inserted by the Jews and Christians into their own books. In particular, the Qur'an negated all the false things attributed to the person of Jesus (peace be upon him) and Mary (peace be upon her), and stated the correct teachings that come from Allah. In this sense the Qur'an has been called muhaymin over the earlier scriptures: it judges the differences among them and makes the decisive statement on all disputed and argumentative matters.

﴿And it is a guidance and mercy for the believers﴾ (27:77). This is the guidance that protects the believers from error and disagreement. It gives them a way of life, supports them on the path of life, and gives them teachings and views that are in harmony with the divine laws (sunan Ilahiyyah) present throughout this universe. This Qur'an is also mercy along with guidance. It saves human beings from doubt, restlessness, anxiety and uncertainty, and protects them from weak views that change day after day, that have no firm footing and cannot stand on their own. Its teachings bring a person, through satisfaction, to the shelter of Allah's mercy and the abode of tranquility. In this way a person harmonizes with his environment, his society and his own thoughts, and lives in peace, and in the Hereafter becomes deserving of Allah's pleasure and great reward. The Qur'anic method for training the human soul and shaping it again according to the laws of nature is a unique method. According to this method, a person lives his life in accordance with those laws of nature which also operate in this universe, and thus his life passes with great tranquility and in a natural way. There is no pretence or artificiality in it. As a result of the Islamic method of training, a person feels contentment even in the depths of his life, and this is a very great wealth. This contentment is attained because, under the Islamic system of training, a person's life does not conflict with the laws of nature, nor does a person conflict with the laws of nature and this universe that moves according to them, nor does human morality conflict with these laws of nature, provided that a person can understand the laws of nature and the principles well, and recognizes the points where human personality and this universe are connected. And a person reaches the conclusion that there is no contradiction between human nature, cosmic nature and the Islamic system of life, but that they are mutually proportionate and in harmony. This is the great peace that is established between the human personality and the vast universe spread around a person, and as a result of this peace human society lives a most tranquil life. And this is the mercy to which the Qur'an points. This is the broader meaning of divine mercy.

After these indications that the Qur'an resolves most of the doctrinal issues of the Children of Israel, removes their disagreements, and gives the believers a natural system of life, granting them great tranquility and peace, Allah now consoles the Prophet ﷺ: his people are unjustly disputing with him. Allah will soon decide this as well, with a decision that no one can reject, because Allah's decisions are based on realities and correct knowledge.

﴿So put your trust in Allah; indeed you are upon the manifest truth﴾ (27:79). Allah has made it obligatory upon Himself to support the truth and make it prevail, just as His other laws operating in this universe are necessary and unalterable. These laws do not stop; likewise truth prevails. However, owing to certain hidden wisdoms of Allah, this victory sometimes comes late, and only Allah knows those wisdoms. There are purposes known only to Allah, yet these sunnah are fulfilled without fail and in the end truth attains victory. This is Allah's promise, and it is never broken. A person's faith cannot be complete unless he believes in the unalterability of this sunnah. The meaning is that for the success of truth there is a time appointed with Allah, and before that time this success cannot come. If people are hasty, that is their own mistake.

The Prophet ﷺ faced great difficulties from his people: they quarrelled over every matter, were obstinate and stubborn, and out of mere enmity they did not accept even things that were evident at first sight. Despite the Messenger's ﷺ struggle and his extremely clear proclamation and preaching, they insisted on disbelief, and they ignored the repeated address of the Qur'an. In the face of all this, he is consoled that he has fulfilled the duty of conveying the message and has committed no fault, but it is those who are alive, whose ears are receptive, who listen to words. The dead never listen. The minds of the dead have died, and they become devoid of reflection. Therefore the dead neither believe nor hear. Your people's hearts and minds have died; hence to speak to them is now as good as not speaking. There is no path left before them to return to guidance. Now leave them to their misguidance, their rebellion and their straying.

﴿Indeed, you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn away and flee, nor can you guide the blind out of their straying. You can make hear only those who believe in Our signs and then submit﴾ (27:80–81).

The Qur'an has portrayed the intellectual and psychological condition of these people in a most remarkable manner. It has given a tangible form to intangible meanings. Heart's stagnation, spiritual deadness, dullness of mind and decline of consciousness are described as if these people were dead and deaf, and the Messenger were calling them while they neither hear nor respond, because the dead neither hear, nor have awareness, nor can respond. Another tangible image is of a person who is deaf, hears nothing at all, and does not even turn his face toward the one calling him, but goes in the opposite direction. No matter how loudly you call such a person, he will not hear. At times the Qur'an presents them in the form of the blind: how can a blind person walk on the right path when he cannot see anything at his next step? In these verses all these forms have been presented in a most embodied and personal manner.

Now, in contrast to these dead, deaf and blind people, stand the believers. They are alive, they hear, and they see.

﴿You can make hear only those who believe in Our signs and then submit﴾ (27:81). That is, you can make hear only those who have life, the faculty of hearing and the faculty of sight. Speak only to such people. These are the signs of life, and consciousness exists among living people. Only those who hear and see can accept the call, and it is the believers alone in whom life, hearing and sight are found. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ worked upon such people; they accepted the call and surrendered.

Islam is a very simple religion, easy to understand, and very close to the sound nature (fitrah salimah). A sound heart and a sound nature accept the Islamic call as soon as they encounter it and submit. They do not then indulge in idle talk and disputation. This is the picture of the believers, and it is such people who should be invited. Such people hasten toward the call as soon as they hear it and believe immediately. Leaving the dead in their place, the caller should reach those people who are ready to accept.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 27, verse 82–90:

Now the discussion turns to the signs of the Hour and to some scenes of the Resurrection. After this, there will be a final comment on this surah. A beast of the earth (Dabbat al-Ard) will speak with those people who do not believe in Allah's cosmic signs. After this comes the scene of gathering and dispersal, where these deniers and disputers will stand in complete silence, quiet and still. Then the human being is also directed towards the signs and evidences of the world, such as the alternation of night and day, to see whether there could be any greater miracle than these. But people are heedless of them. Then it is told that when the Trumpet is blown, these people will be in great distress and wailing, and will cry out, but to no benefit. When the mountains will move and these people will be flying in the expanse of the universe like clouds, then it is told that some people will not be affected by this distress and terror, and will stand completely at peace, while some others will be extremely terrified and bowed down. And in that very state they will be thrown into Hell.

﴿And when the Word falls upon them...﴾ to ﴿...only what you used to do will you be recompensed?﴾ (82-90)

"، ۔ "۔۔۔۔ , "۔ The emergence of a beast from the earth is mentioned in some hadiths. But in those authentic narrations there are no details or attributes of that beast. The narrations that describe some attributes of that beast have not reached the level of authenticity, so we here set aside those attributes. Because whether the length of the beast is seven yards, or that it is hairy, or that it has a beard, or that its head is like an ox, or that its eyes are like those of a pig, or that its ears are like those of an elephant, or its horns are like those of a stag, or its neck is like that of a gazelle, and its chest is like that of a lion, and its color is like that of a leopard, and its two sides are like those of a cat, and its tail is like that of a ram, its feet are like those of a camel, and it has wings and hooves, is not an important matter. These are the attributes about which the commentators became perplexed.

So we should suffice with the Qur'anic text and authentic hadiths, and believe that one of the signs of the Hour is that such a beast will emerge, and this will happen when the doors of repentance are closed. At that time, the decision will be final for those who are present, and there will be no opportunity left for them to repent. Then, whatever state and belief people are upon, a decision will be made about them. At that time this beast will emerge. It will speak with them, whereas generally beasts do not speak, or we do not understand their speech. But today all people will understand the speech of this beast, and will know that this is the miracle that was to come before the Hour. Before this, they did not believe in the signs of Allah, nor did they affirm them, nor did they affirm the Hour.

It should be kept in view here that Surah al-Naml mentions such observations and wonders, such as the conversation of insects of the earth, the conversation of birds, the conversation of jinn, and Solomon (peace be upon him) understanding their speech. In this context, the beast of the earth and its speech with people is an expression of harmony of the subject matter. Thus the Qur'an brings scenes, examples and subjects, meanings and concepts that are harmonious and consistent with one another in every surah. (See my book al-Tasweer al-Fanni.)

Now, after the description of the sign of the beast of the earth, the discussion enters into the scenes of the Resurrection itself.

﴿And on the day when We gather from every nation a host of those who denied Our signs, and they will be marshaled...﴾ (27:83) "And imagine the day when We shall gather from every community a host of those who used to deny Our signs, and then they will be arranged in order." All people will be raised. Allah's will was thus so that He might make the position of the deniers clear. The word yūzaʿūn means that they will all be driven in an orderly arrangement, they will have no choice or will of their own, and they will not be able to go anywhere according to their own wish.

﴿Until, when they arrive, He will say, "Did you deny My signs while you did not comprehend them in knowledge? Or what was it that you were doing?"﴾ (27:84) "Until when they all arrive, He will say: Did you deny My signs although you had not encompassed their knowledge? If not this, then what were you doing?" The first question is asked to put them to shame and reproach them, because it was already known and well established that they had denied. As for the second question, it is a thorough sarcasm upon their lives. Examples of this style of address exist in every language: Did you deny, or what did you used to do? Because apparently your life has no purpose visible. That is, apart from denial, no other action of your life is known, whereas you ought not to have denied. Such questions do not receive an answer, because the answer is evident, so the addressee remains silent. Indeed, because of this very question the addressee becomes speechless and cannot form any reply.

﴿And the word will fall upon them because of their wrongdoing, and they will not be able to speak﴾ (27:85) "And because of their wrongdoing the promise of punishment will be fulfilled upon them, and then they will not be able to say anything." That is, because of oppression and associating partners in the world, the decision against them becomes just, and now they stand helpless, speechless and silent. This will happen when the beast speaks and people cannot speak. This is one aspect of the miraculous style of the Qur'an: it creates a beautiful contrast of meaning within speech, that the beast is speaking, it has a tongue in its mouth, while these humans, though human, are without speech. Furthermore, there is also a blending and contrast here between the observed world and the observed Resurrection. Sometimes the scene of the world comes before us, and sometimes that of the Hereafter, because the emergence of the beast will be during the final days of the world. And thus a deep impression is created in the atmosphere.

Here first is the scene of the Resurrection, where the deniers stand stunned and speechless. Then the discourse moves to the world, and their conscience and awareness are awakened, and they are invited to reflect upon this order of the universe, how great is the power of the Lord of the worlds, who provides for you all the means of life. He provides for you the means of comfort and rest in the world. He has made the whole universe so supportive that your life passes very happily within it. This universe and its forces are aids to life, not harmful to life. They are supportive of human life, not at war with it.

﴿Did they not see that We made the night for them to rest in, and the day to give light? Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe﴾ (27:86) "Did they not see that We made the night for them to find tranquility, and made the day bright? Surely there are signs in that for those who believe." The scene of the night is perfectly calm and silent, and the day is bright and speaking. And this scene is capable of creating within a human being such awareness and intuition that connects him to Allah, who is the One who sets night and day in motion. The scenes of night and day are in fact two cosmic proofs, and they are sufficient for those who wish to believe, but they do not believe.

If there were no night, the whole time would be day, and life would not be possible on this earth; and similarly, if there were continuous night, life would also not be possible. Indeed, even if night and day were ten times longer than their present duration, life on this earth would become impossible. The sun would scorch all vegetation, and the night would freeze everything. Therefore the alternation of night and day is also a means of life for human beings, yet people do not believe.

Now from the scene of these two proofs and miracles of the alternation of night and day, the discourse in the blink of an eye moves to the scenes of the Resurrection. A moment earlier, humans were living a happy and joyful life on this earth, when the Trumpet was blown. A tremor came between the heavens and the earth. All creatures, except those whom Allah wills, became frightened. The mountains began to move from their places, although they were symbols of stability and tranquility. Then on that day the fates of people became visible. For someone the end was peace and security, and for someone it reached wailing and being thrown face-down into the fire.

﴿And the day the Trumpet is blown, those in the heavens and those on the earth will be terrified, except whom Allah wills...﴾ (27:87-90) "And how will it be on the day when the Trumpet is blown and those who are in the heavens and the earth will be struck with terror, except those whom Allah wills to save... and all will come to Him in humility. You see the mountains and think them firmly fixed, but on that day they will pass away like clouds. This is the handiwork of Allah, who has perfected everything. Indeed He is Well-Aware of what you do. Whoever comes with good will have better than it, and such people will be secure from the terror of that day, and whoever comes with evil, such will be thrown face-down into the Fire. Will you be recompensed except for what you used to do?"

The Trumpet is the horn into which the blast will be blown on the Day of Resurrection. This will be the sound by which all creatures of the heavens and the earth will be terrified, unless Allah keeps someone safe from it. It has been said that the martyrs will be safe from it. All living creation will swoon or die. Then it will be blown a second time, and all people will be instantly revived. ﴿And all will come to Him in humility﴾ (27:87): that is, they will be completely obedient, with heads bowed. With this terror the existing order of the heavens will be disturbed, and the mountains will fly like tufts of wool. All orbits will end, and the mountains will move like clouds and scatter. Just as people will be agitated, so the mountains too will be agitated. There will be disorder among living beings and inanimate things alike; it will be as if the mountains too become frightened and run about bewildered and distressed. Their movement will have neither direction nor stability, like the movement of living things.

﴿This is the handiwork of Allah, who has perfected everything﴾ (27:88) "This is the handiwork of Allah, who has perfected everything." Glory be to Allah, the beauty and perfection of His craftsmanship is manifest in all His creations. Every action of His happens at the right time; there is in it no flaw, no chance or coincidence, no rebellion, and Allah has not left anything in it to chance. Whatever thing He created, He completed its benefit and harm. He made everything purposeful. Every small and large thing is placed according to a measure, in accordance with a plan and purpose, and within it there is such deep wisdom and precise planning that minds are dazzled. For further details, see the commentary on the verse "khalaqa kulla shay'" in Surah al-Furqan.

﴿Indeed He is Aware of what you do﴾ (27:88) "Indeed He is Well-Aware of what you do." This is the Day of Reckoning, for the deeds that you used to do in the world. This day has been appointed by the One whose power is manifested in this entire universe. Allah brings it at its appointed time; there can be no advancement or delay of even an hour in it, because He created everything with wisdom, and everything must play its role according to His wisdom, so that the divine scheme of action and its recompense may reach its conclusion. Action is in the first life, and its reward and recompense is in the second life.

﴿This is the handiwork of Allah... Indeed He is Well-Aware of what you do﴾ (27:88): On that terrifying and dreadful day, those who did good deeds in the life of the world will be in perfect peace and tranquility. And beyond this peace and security, the reward and recompense they receive will be very great and sufficient.

﴿Whoever comes with good will have better than it, and such people will be secure from the terror of that day﴾ (27:89): To remain safe from the terror of the Day of Resurrection is itself the full reward of our humble deeds. The favours and honours that follow are, as it were, a gift and a pension. This is because the people of piety used to fear Allah in the world as well, but they did not think it appropriate to combine the terror of the Hereafter with the fear and piety of Allah in the world. Rather, Allah has excepted the people of piety from it. On that day, whatever creature is in the heavens and the earth will be affected by this terror, except those whom Allah has saved, and they are the God-fearing.

﴿And whoever comes with evil, such will be thrown face-down into the Fire﴾ (27:90): This is an extremely frightening scene, in which people are dragged to the edge of Hell and thrown face-down into it, while they are further rebuked and reproached.

﴿Will you be recompensed except for what you used to do?﴾ (27:90): Earlier, in the world, they turned away from guidance and denied it. Therefore here, as punishment, they are being thrown face-down into the Fire, because the truth had come before them very clearly and openly, as plain as night and day, yet they turned away.

﴿Will you be recompensed except for what you used to do?﴾ (27:90): Earlier, in the world, they turned away from guidance and denied it. Therefore here, as punishment, they are being thrown face-down into the Fire, because the truth had come before them very clearly and openly, as plain as night and day, yet they turned away.

Now at the very end of the surah come the final blows. Here the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is told to set out the summary of his call, to explain his method of work and to describe the manner of his invitation. Having conveyed the message and delivered the word of God, he is to leave these people to the end that Allah has chosen for them, because they themselves have chosen it for themselves. And the matter closes with the same praise with which it began.

These were the basic elements of the Islamic call. As for its means and its vehicle, that is the recitation of the Qur'an.

﴿And that I should recite the Qur'an.﴾ (27: 92) The Qur'an is, in essence, the first book of the Islamic call. It is our constitution and the means of our success and salvation. The Prophet ﷺ has been commanded to wage jihad with this Qur'an against the disbelievers. It contains much for the training of human reason and the human soul. It takes hold of every aspect of the human self. It tests all the ways of human consciousness. It has such power that it sets hard hearts trembling. It shakes the human heart and mind so profoundly that it leaves them restless. For the Islamic call, the Qur'an is sufficient and healing. Jihad and fighting have been made obligatory only so that the believers may be protected from the trials and the evil of enemies, and so that there is no obstacle in the way of the Qur'anic call throughout the world. A second purpose of jihad is the acquisition of a power through which the Shari'ah may enforce its law. As for the Islamic call, its means and vehicle is the Book of Allah alone. ﴿I have been commanded to recite the Qur'an.﴾ (27: 92)

﴿Whoever is guided, is guided only for his own benefit; and whoever goes astray, say: I am only a warner.﴾ (27: 92) This verse states the principle of individual responsibility: every person is himself responsible in choosing the path of guidance or misguidance. Within this principle of individual responsibility operates the principle that, in the sight of Allah, the human being is highly honoured, and Islam attaches great importance to the dignity of man. Islam does not drive people like animals into the fold of Islam by compulsion. Islam presents the call of Islam before people in the form of the Qur'an, invites them to reflection, and this call touches the hearts of people. This is the profound, excellent and deep method of Islam, which takes human nature from its very depths, just as the Qur'an has adopted a most natural method for the training of human souls.

﴿And say: All praise is for Allah.﴾ (27: 93) Praise of Allah before His perfections and His wonders.

﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what you do.﴾ (27: 93) This is the final blow laid upon the strings of human intellect and understanding at the end of this surah: in a most sweet, beautiful and allusive manner, and then in a most decisive and frightening style of expression.
